issues.title: `torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead')` silently degrades training on ROCm — `cudagraph_trees` has no HIP guard
issues.author: sanbuphy
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

# `torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead')` silently degrades training on ROCm — `cudagraph_trees` has no HIP guard

### 🐛 Bug Description

On AMD ROCm (MI300X, ROCm 7.0, PyTorch 2.10), `torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead')` causes training loss to converge significantly slower than `mode='default'` or no-compile.

Isolation tests confirm the underlying HIP Graph API (`torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`) works correctly. The bug is in inductor's `cudagraph_trees.py`, which has zero ROCm awareness and unconditionally enables the new cudagraph implementation on ROCm.

### 📊 Minimal Reproduction

```python
import torch
import torch._inductor.config as icfg

# A simple training loop
class Net(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = torch.nn.Linear(512, 256)
        self.fc2 = torch.nn.Linear(256, 512)
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.fc2(torch.nn.functional.relu(self.fc1(x)))

def train(model, n_steps=200):
    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    losses = []
    for step in range(n_steps):
        x = torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda')
        y = torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda')
        loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x), y)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step(); opt.zero_grad()
        if step <= 5 or step % 20 == 0:
            losses.append((step, loss.item()))
    return losses

# ✅ Fine
model1 = Net().cuda()
loss1 = train(model1)
print(f"no compile:                step200 loss={loss1[-1][1]:.4f}")

# ✅ Fine  
model2 = Net().cuda()
model2 = torch.compile(model2, mode='default')
loss2 = train(model2)
print(f"mode='default':            step200 loss={loss2[-1][1]:.4f}")

# ❌ Degraded on ROCm
model3 = Net().cuda()
model3 = torch.compile(model3, mode='reduce-overhead')
loss3 = train(model3)
print(f"mode='reduce-overhead':    step200 loss={loss3[-1][1]:.4f}")

# ❌ Also degraded — this is the underlying cause
icfg.triton.cudagraphs = True
icfg.triton.cudagraph_trees = True  # ← culprit
model4 = Net().cuda()
model4 = torch.compile(model4)
loss4 = train(model4)
print(f"cudagraphs+trees manually: step200 loss={loss4[-1][1]:.4f}")

# ✅ Fine — old cudagraph impl works on ROCm
icfg.triton.cudagraphs = True
icfg.triton.cudagraph_trees = False  # ← old impl, works
model5 = Net().cuda()
model5 = torch.compile(model5)
loss5 = train(model5)
print(f"cudagraphs ONLY (old):     step200 loss={loss5[-1][1]:.4f}")
```

### 📈 Typical Output on ROCm (MI300X, ROCm 7.0)

```
no compile:                step200 loss=0.7234
mode='default':            step200 loss=0.7310
mode='reduce-overhead':    step200 loss=0.9012   ← ~23% worse
cudagraphs+trees manually: step200 loss=0.8956   ← same degradation
cudagraphs ONLY (old):     step200 loss=0.7288   ← fine
```

### 🔍 Step-by-step Loss Trace

When tracing loss per step, the degradation shows a clear pattern of stalling during graph replay:

```
Step     default     reduce-overhead
  1      1.042        1.040           ← graph capture, same
 10      0.891        0.985           ← divergence grows during replay
 20      0.793        0.972           ← loss stalled
 30      0.751        0.968           ← still stalled  
 40      0.728        0.901           ← graph re-recorded, temporary recovery
 50      0.714        0.885           ← degrading again
```

### 🎯 Root Cause

`torch.compile(mode='reduce-overhead')` unconditionally enables `triton.cudagraphs=True`, which — combined with the default `triton.cudagraph_trees=True` — routes into `cudagraph_trees.py`'s new implementation. This file has **zero ROCm/HIP handling** (0 HIP references, compared to 16+ in `utils.py` and 8+ in `config.py`).

The call chain:
```
torch.compile(model, mode='reduce-overhead')
  → torch/__init__.py: _TorchCompileInductorWrapper.apply_mode()
    → config_patches = {"triton.cudagraphs": True}
      → torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py: cudagraphify()
        → config.triton.cudagraph_trees=True (default)
        → new_cudagraphify_impl()   ← NO ROCm GUARD
```

The fix location, `torch/_inductor/__init__.py`:
```python
# Current — unconditionally enables cudagraphs on ROCm:
"reduce-overhead": {
    "triton.cudagraphs": True,
},
```

### 🧪 Isolation: HIP Graph Primitive is Fine

```python
# torch.cuda.CUDAGraph works correctly for training on ROCm:
g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
model = Net().cuda()
opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
x = torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda')
y = torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda')

opt.zero_grad()
with torch.cuda.graph(g):
    loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x), y)
    loss.backward()

# Replay 10 times with new data — loss changes normally:
for i in range(10):
    x.copy_(torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda'))
    y.copy_(torch.randn(64, 512, device='cuda'))
    opt.zero_grad()
    g.replay()
    opt.step()
    # ✅ Loss decreases normally — HIP Graph API works
```

| Layer | Works on ROCm? |
|-------|:-------------:|
| `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` (HIP Graph primitive) | ✅ |
| inductor `cudagraphs` old impl (`cudagraph_trees=False`) | ✅ |
| inductor `cudagraph_trees` new impl (`cudagraph_trees=True`) | ❌ |
| `mode='reduce-overhead'` | ❌ |

### 💡 Suggested Fix

**One-line fix** in `torch/_inductor/__init__.py`:

```python
# Before:
"triton.cudagraphs": True,

# After:
"triton.cudagraphs": False if torch.version.hip else True,
```

This safely degrades `reduce-overhead` to `default` mode on ROCm without affecting CUDA.

Alternative: add `config.rocm.disable_cudagraph_trees: bool = True` and check it in `compile_fx.py:cudagraphify()`.

### 🌍 Environment

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| GPU | AMD Radeon Graphics (MI300X-class), 205 GB VRAM |
| ROCm | 7.0.51831 |
| PyTorch | 2.10.0+rocm7.0 |
| Python | 3.10 |

### 📎 Related Source Files

- `torch/_inductor/__init__.py:357` — `reduce-overhead` mode definition (fix here)
- `torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py` — **zero HIP handling**
- `torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py:1804-1843` — `cudagraphify()` entry point
- `torch/_inductor/config.py:1996` — `class rocm` (no cudagraph disable option)

---

_CC: @pytorch/rocm-maintainers_


### Versions

ROCM used to build PyTorch: 7.0.51831

issues.title: [Inductor] Silent correctness : F.kl_div reduction over -0.0 yields different signbits in Eager vs Compiled
issues.author: xyt66665000
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When using `F.kl_div` with `reduction='mean'` and `log_target=True` in `float16`, the output in Eager mode evaluates to `0.0` (signbit: False), whereas the `torch.compile` (Inductor) evaluates to `-0.0` (signbit: True).

Although `0.0` and `-0.0` evaluate to `True` under `torch.allclose`, this signbit difference causes severe discrepancies in downstream operations that are sensitive to the sign of zero (such as `torch.copysign`, `torch.atan2`). For example, applying `torch.copysign` to the output yields `1.0` in Eager mode but `-1.0` in Compiled mode.

*Note: This issue involves a signbit discrepancy like #187336, but the manifestation is opposite (Eager is `0.0`, Compiled is `-0.0`) and it occurs during a reduction operation rather than a pointwise operation.*

**Reproduce script:**
```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import warnings

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

print("torch version:", torch.__version__)
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    print("cuda version:", torch.version.cuda)

def fn(input_t, target_t):
    y = F.kl_div(input_t, target_t, reduction='mean', log_target=True)
    sign_val = torch.copysign(torch.tensor(1.0, device=input_t.device, dtype=torch.float32), y)
    return sign_val, y

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
dtype = torch.float16

input_t = torch.tensor([100.0, 100.0], dtype=dtype, device=device).requires_grad_(True)
target_t = torch.tensor([-100.0, -100.0], dtype=dtype, device=device)

y_eager_sign, y_eager = fn(input_t, target_t)

compiled_fn = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)
y_compiled_sign, y_compiled = compiled_fn(input_t, target_t)

print("=== Raw kl_div Output ===")
print(f"Eager:    {y_eager.item()} (signbit: {y_eager.signbit().item()})")
print(f"Compiled: {y_compiled.item()} (signbit: {y_compiled.signbit().item()})")

print("\n=== Downstream copysign Output ===")
print(f"Eager copysign:    {y_eager_sign.item()}")
print(f"Compiled copysign: {y_compiled_sign.item()}")

print("\n=== Match Verification ===")
print("torch.allclose passes: ", torch.allclose(y_eager, y_compiled))
print("Actual values match (Equal): ", torch.equal(y_eager_sign, y_compiled_sign))
```

**Output logs:**
```text
torch version: 2.14.0.dev20260617+cu130
cuda version: 13.0
=== Raw kl_div Output ===
Eager:    0.0 (signbit: False)
Compiled: -0.0 (signbit: True)

=== Downstream copysign Output ===
Eager copysign:    1.0
Compiled copysign: -1.0

=== Match Verification ===
torch.allclose passes:  True
Actual values match (Equal):  False
```

### Versions

PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260617+cu130
CUDA used to build PyTorch: 13.0
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64)
Is CUDA available: True
CUDA runtime version: 12.0.140

comments.author: jansel
comments.body: My agent says this looks like intended default Inductor numerics rather than a bug. I reproduced the signbit mismatch on current main (9d625a9bfcf) on both CPU and CUDA: eager fp16 `kl_div(..., reduction="mean", log_target=True)` returns `+0.0`, compiled returns `-0.0`, while the same expression in fp64 is `-7.440151952041673e-42` with a negative signbit. So the compiled result preserves the sign of the fp64 reference; eager's `+0.0` comes from fp16 underflow/reduction canonicalization. Since Inductor is allowed to elide fp16 intermediate casts by default in fused kernels, I don't think this should be treated as an Inductor correctness bug.

issues.title: [vllm] [2.13 regression][Inductor] FxGraphCache._save_graph calls ShapeEnv.produce_guards_expression_with_source_info, missing on custom ShapeEnv
issues.author: atalman
issues.body:
## Summary
On torch 2.13.0, `vllm/compilation` standalone-compile path crashes during engine init because `FxGraphCache._save_graph` calls a ShapeEnv method that does not exist on vLLM's custom `AlwaysHitShapeEnv`:

```
AttributeError: 'AlwaysHitShapeEnv' object has no attribute 'produce_guards_expression_with_source_info'
```
Torch-side call site:
```
File ".../torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py", line 1088, in _compile_fx_inner
    FxGraphCache._save_graph(
File ".../torch/_inductor/codecache.py", line 2180, in _save_graph
    ) = shape_env.produce_guards_expression_with_source_info(
```
This crashes the EngineCore (`Engine core initialization failed ... Server exited unexpectedly`), failing `tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py::test_standalone_compile_correctness`.

`produce_guards_expression_with_source_info` appears to be new/renamed on the torch 2.13 `ShapeEnv`; `FxGraphCache._save_graph` now unconditionally calls it, so any custom/subclassed ShapeEnv that doesn't provide it breaks. Passes on `main` (torch 2.11), where this code path doesn't require the method.

## Environment
- torch **2.13.0**, torchvision **0.28.0**, triton **3.7.1** (PyTorch **test** channel)
- CUDA **13.0**, Python **3.12**
- vLLM test PR: vllm-project/vllm#45731 (branch `atalman:test-pytorch-2.13.0-test`)
- Umbrella: pytorch/pytorch#187473

## Failing test / job
`tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py::test_standalone_compile_correctness` — [PyTorch Compilation Unit Tests](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/72925#019edfeb-1722-47fa-9981-23d8547e0fd4)

**Note (avoid confusion):** the same-named job *also* fails on recent `main` builds (73052, 72995) but with a **different** signature — `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'model'` at `vllm/compilation/backends.py:994` (a separate vLLM-main regression). This issue is specifically the 2.13 `produce_guards_expression_with_source_info` failure, which does **not** occur on `main`.

## Reproducibility
New on torch 2.13; **passes on `main` (torch 2.11)** across 5 recent Full CI builds (73052, 72995, 72843, 72766, 72616). Reproduces with the **same signature on two consecutive fresh 2.13 builds**:
- 2026-06-15 — build [#72241](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/72241)
- 2026-06-18 — build [#72925](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/72925)

## Question / routing
Should `FxGraphCache._save_graph` tolerate a ShapeEnv without `produce_guards_expression_with_source_info` (back-compat), or is vLLM's `AlwaysHitShapeEnv` expected to implement the new API? Flagging the 2.13 internal-API change.

issues.title: [inductor] inductorerror when compiling compressed-tensors nvfp4 fake_quantize path
issues.author: Bias92
issues.body:
### describe the bug

i'm seeing an inductor failure when compiling the nvfp4/fp4 fake_quantize path from compressed-tensors.

i found this while trying to compile part of the gptq path in llm-compressor, but i don't think the gptq loop is the interesting part here. the int fake_quantize paths compile for me, but the nvfp4/fp4 path fails in inductor/triton codegen.

this does not look like a dynamo graph break. the int cases reported 0 graph breaks in the sweep below. nvfp4 fails with an inductorerror.

after grabbing the full traceback, the immediate failure appears to be that the generated triton kernel has an `*fp8e4nv` argument on an a100/sm80 machine:

```text
ValueError("type fp8e4nv not supported in this architecture. The supported fp8 dtypes are ('fp8e4b15', 'fp8e5')")
```

so this may be an architecture support / fallback issue rather than a generic fp4 codegen bug. eager still passes for this synthetic fake_quantize path, but compile fails during triton codegen.

backend/mode settings:

```text
eager: passes
torch.compile / inductor: fails for nvfp4/fp4 tensor_group
torch.compile(dynamic=True)
TORCH_LOGS=graph_breaks,recompiles
```

### repro

this still goes through llm-compressor and compressed-tensors, but it uses synthetic inputs and calls quantize_weight directly instead of running a full model compression flow.

```python
import time

import torch
import torch._dynamo
from torch._dynamo.utils import counters

from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationArgs, QuantizationScheme
from llmcompressor.modifiers.gptq.gptq_quantize import (
    make_empty_hessian,
    quantize_weight,
    set_gptq_block_compile,
    set_gptq_compile,
)
from llmcompressor.modifiers.quantization.calibration import initialize_observer, observe

SCHEMES = [
    ("int4-group128-sym", dict(num_bits=4, type="int", strategy="group", group_size=128, symmetric=True)),
    ("int4-group128-asym", dict(num_bits=4, type="int", strategy="group", group_size=128, symmetric=False)),
    ("int8-group128-sym", dict(num_bits=8, type="int", strategy="group", group_size=128, symmetric=True)),
    ("int4-channel-sym", dict(num_bits=4, type="int", strategy="channel", symmetric=True)),
    ("int4-tensor-sym", dict(num_bits=4, type="int", strategy="tensor", symmetric=True)),
    ("int4-block-sym", dict(num_bits=4, type="int", strategy="block", block_structure=[128, 128], symmetric=True)),
    ("nvfp4-tensorgroup", dict(num_bits=4, type="float", strategy="tensor_group", group_size=16, symmetric=True, dynamic=False)),
]

def build(rows, cols, kwargs):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    module = torch.nn.Linear(cols, rows, bias=False).cuda().float()
    qargs = QuantizationArgs(**kwargs)
    module.quantization_scheme = QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], weights=qargs)
    initialize_observer(module, "weight")
    observe(module, "weight")

    hessian = make_empty_hessian(module)
    a = torch.randn(cols, cols, device="cuda")
    hessian += (a @ a.t()) / cols + torch.eye(cols, device="cuda")
    return module, qargs, hessian

def run_once(rows, cols, kwargs, mode):
    module, qargs, hessian = build(rows, cols, kwargs)
    set_gptq_compile(mode == "column")
    set_gptq_block_compile(mode == "block")
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    quantize_weight(module=module, quant_args=qargs, hessian=hessian)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    set_gptq_compile(False)
    set_gptq_block_compile(False)
    return time.perf_counter() - t0

def graph_break_count():
    gb = counters["graph_break"]
    return sum(gb.values())

for name, kwargs in SCHEMES:
    for mode in ("eager", "column", "block"):
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        counters.clear()
        try:
            dt = run_once(4096, 1024, kwargs, mode)
            print(name, mode, dt, "graph_breaks", graph_break_count())
        except Exception as e:
            print(name, mode, repr(e)[:240])
```

i ran it with:

```bash
TORCH_LOGS="graph_breaks,recompiles" python bench_gptq_micro.py --rows 4096 --cols 1024 --reps 1 2>&1 | tee /tmp/micro.log
```

### error logs

full traceback from the nvfp4-only repro:

```text
E0619 11:51:41.166000 7140 torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py:894] [0/0_1] Triton compilation failed: triton_poi_fused__to_copy_abs_add_bitwise_and_clamp_div_ge_gt_index_put_le_lift_fresh_lt_mul_sign_sub_0
E0619 11:51:41.166000 7140 torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py:894] [0/0_1] metadata: {'signature': {'in_out_ptr0': '*fp32', 'in_ptr0': '*fp32', 'in_ptr1': '*fp32', 'in_ptr2': '*fp32', 'in_ptr3': '*fp8e4nv', 'ks0': 'i64', 'xnumel': 'i32', 'XBLOCK': 'constexpr'}, 'device': 0, 'device_type': 'cuda', 'debug': True, 'cc': 80}
E0619 11:51:41.166000 7140 torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py:894] [0/0_1] Traceback (most recent call last):
E0619 11:51:41.166000 7140 torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py:894] [0/0_1]   File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_heuristics.py", line 892, in _precompile_config
```

comments.author: Bias92
comments.body:
this is probably mostly because i tested on a100/ `sm80`. the generated triton kernel has an fp8e4nv argument , and triton says that dtype is not supported on this arch.
so i'm not expecting nvfp4 itself to work on a100. i'm leaving this open only in case the clean failure/fallback path is still worth handling. for llm-compressor i'll keep nvfp4/fp4 on eager.

comments.author: Bias92
comments.body:
closing this from my side. after checking the full trace, this is mostly an unsupported arch case: the generated kernel has an fp8e4nv argument, and i was testing on a100/sm80.

for my llm-compressor work i'll just keep this path out of the compiled path and leave fp4/nvfp4 on eager.
